newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to invest $708 mln in two new power plants.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to invest $708 mln in two new power plants.

text.p: The Turkish state electricity utility TEAS is planning to invest $708 million in the construction of two coal-fired power plants in western Turkey, energy officials said on Wednesday.

Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan told reporters that of the two lignite-powered plants in Kutahya province, one at Tuncbilek would have a capacity of 300 MegaWatts (MW) and another at Seyitomer would have a capacity of 150 MW.
He said the planned plants would go into production after the year 2000 and would provide 300 jobs.

"This investment also requires new investment in coalfields. We planned new investment of $250 million in coalfields in the region of Tuncbilek and Seyitomer," Kutan said. He said this investment would provide employment for 2,100 workers.
At Tuncbilek there is already a plant with a capacity of 429 MW and at Seyitomer there is a plant with a 700 MW capacity.
Kutan also said Turkey's demand for lignite will rise from 63 million tonnes to 113 million tonnes by the year 2000.
He added that by the year 2010 Turkey's imports will rise to 60 percent of energy demands from 52 percent currently.
TEAS general manager Afif Demirkiran said the tenders for the new plants wuld be issued this year.
Turkey's power demand grew 12 percent in 1996.
